Handoff mechanics: on Windows, GNU patch without --binary rejects every hunk ('different line endings'). Apply with `git apply .claude/agents_shared/reports/wordnew-native-build_apk.diff` from the repo root (verified with --check) or `patch --binary -p1`. The expected result is sha256 7681c09e....

keystore_is_complete checks JKS/JCEKS by the 4-byte magic only. The lead re-ran it: the first 76-char base64 line of a JKS decodes to 57 bytes and is accepted, while the same truncation of a PKCS12 is rejected. Gradle would then fail at signing, after vite and sync, and no bad APK is produced. Optional fix: accept PKCS12 only (keytool's default), or state the limit.

SECRET_DECRYPT_STEP names `ensure_secret_keys_ready`, which is the Linux function (secret_functions.sh:437, dd.sh:52). On Windows, dd.cmd runs win_common/SecretDecryptionCheck.ps1 (dd.ps1:1176), so the message is only approximate there (B11 parity). A one-constant fix naming both steps can be made when the diff is applied or in a wordnew-native follow-up.

`repo_root = root.parents[1]` (diff main) raises IndexError on every build type when --root is shallow, e.g. `--root D:/ui`. The real layout is always deep, so this is an edge case. Computing it only for release, or from script_dir, would remove it.
